subject: Physics
source: Phase F · FEAT-PF1 — author-original scaffold rows for the highest-volume Edexcel Y10 physics spec points (1PH0).

sentenceFrames: I will use Newton's second law: F = m × a.

wordBank.definition: a push or pull, measured in newtons (N)
the amount of matter in an object, measured in kilograms (kg)
rate of change of velocity, measured in m/s²
F = ma — the resultant force on an object equals mass times acceleration

stepLadder: Identify the resultant force and the mass from the question.
Rearrange to a = F/m if acceleration is the unknown.
Give the answer with the unit m/s².
commonPitfalls: Using weight instead of mass (or vice versa).
Forgetting to subtract opposing forces to get the resultant force.

wordBank.definition: the number of complete waves per second, measured in hertz (Hz)
the distance between two adjacent peaks of a wave, measured in metres
how fast the wave travels, measured in m/s

stepLadder: Write the wave equation v = fλ.
Identify the frequency in Hz and the wavelength in m.
Multiply to find the wave speed.
Give the answer with the unit m/s.
Sense-check: visible waves on water are typically less than 1 m/s; light is much faster.
commonPitfalls: Mixing units — converting cm to m is a common slip.
